profile.overview: Crystal Crop Protection Limited is an agrochemical and seed company established in 1994. The company develops, manufactures, and distributes crop protection products, natural crop solutions, technical-grade active ingredients, and seeds. Its crop protection portfolio includes herbicides, fungicides, insecticides, bio-stimulants, bio-protectants, plant growth regulators, liquid fertilisers, and micronutrients. Its seed portfolio covers field crops such as cotton, mustard, maize, rice, and wheat, along with vegetable and flower seeds. The company also manufactures self-propelled boom sprayers and sells conventional sprayers. It operates four formulation manufacturing units in Haryana, Gujarat, and Jammu and two technical manufacturing units in Gujarat and Maharashtra. Its seed processing facilities are located in Hyderabad, Telangana, and Bengaluru, Karnataka. The company also operates research and development facilities across multiple states, including its Key Research and Development Centre in Sonipat, Haryana.
profile.productsAndServices: Crop protection chemicals, insecticides, fungicides, bio-stimulants, hybrid field seeds, and agricultural sprayers.
profile.businessModel: Integrated B2B technical active ingredient synthesis and B2C branded formulations distributed across 15,000+ retail agri-dealers pan-India.
profile.industryOverview: Indian agrochemicals and seed solutions market benefiting from crop yield intensification and export substitution.
profile.competitivePosition: Top-tier domestic formulation player with multi-regional manufacturing and extensive field agronomist outreach.
growthOpportunities: Expansion into biological crop solutions and organic bio-stimulants
Scaling hybrid seed sales in cotton, mustard, and maize belts
Increasing direct farm mechanization sprayer penetration
strengths: Over 30 years of operational track record in Indian agricultural formulations and technical actives.
Diversified portfolio across crop protection, seeds, plant nutrition, and mechanization sprayers.
Four formulation units and two technical manufacturing plants with in-house R&D at Sonipat, Haryana.
risks: Agrochemical demand is seasonal and linked to monsoon patterns, rainfall distribution, and farm realizations.
Subject to stringent environmental clearances and regulatory approvals for active ingredient formulations.
Significant trade receivables and raw material price volatility linked to global chemical intermediates.

profile.overview: Vedant Poly Fabs Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of flexible packaging materials and supplies to business-to-business (B2B) customers across India. Its product portfolio includes 3-layer and 5-layer low-density (LD) films, shrink films, barrier films, printed laminates, and milk and oil pouches used in food and beverage and other consumer product packaging. The company manufactures products according to customer specifications, including size, thickness, material composition, and printing requirements. Its manufacturing processes include extrusion, printing, lamination, slitting, and pouching. The facility is equipped with multilayer extrusion machines, central impression (CI) flexographic printing machines, and rotogravure printing machines. In addition to manufacturing, the company trades in billet strips used in engineering, fabrication, and manufacturing industries. It commenced operations in 2018 and expanded its manufacturing capacity in March 2024 by adding lamination, slitting, and pouching machines. The company also operates a reprocessing unit to process plastic waste generated during manufacturing for reuse in certain applications.

profile.overview: Zepto Limited is the fastest-growing quick commerce platform in India, focused on delivering groceries, fruits, vegetables, and a wide assortment of household products to users in under 10 minutes. The company operates a marketplace model, leveraging a network of over 1,139 strategically located 'dark stores' as of March 2026. Its business model relies on a proprietary technology stack for its app, warehouse management, last-mile delivery, and brand advertising, serving both end-consumers and providing B2B services to wholesalers and retailers.
profile.productsAndServices: Zepto operates in its core segment (Founded 2020).
profile.businessModel: Mainboard issue (EQUITY) listed on NSE / BSE · ISIN ZEPTOISIN123.
profile.industryOverview: Sector primary market offering tracked via SEBI & exchange filings.
profile.competitivePosition: Bidding dates to be announced
strengths: As India's fastest-growing quick commerce platform, Zepto's order volume grew at a CAGR of approximately 119.50% between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026, significantly outpacing the industry. This market leadership is mirrored in its financial performance, with revenue from operations skyrocketing from ₹4,454.52 Crores in FY24 to ₹22,623.58 Crores in FY26.

The company's 'densification flywheel' strategy is improving operational efficiency, evidenced by the Average Distance per Order decreasing from 2.05 km in FY24 to 1.78 km in FY26, while the Orders Per Day (OPD) per store increased from 1,325 to 1,677 in the same period.

Zepto is demonstrating significant improvements in unit economics, with Fixed Cost per Order reducing from ₹80.72 in Q1 FY24 to ₹52.34 in Q4 FY26. Concurrently, Digital Marketing Cost per Order has dramatically decreased from ₹10.82 to ₹1.01 in the same period, indicating increased brand salience and user retention.

The company is successfully monetizing its platform beyond delivery commissions, with high-margin Advertisement Revenue growing exponentially from ₹49.17 Crores in FY24 to ₹1,635.73 Crores in FY26, a CAGR of 477.9%. This segment now constitutes 7.23% of total revenue from operations in FY26.

Leveraging its data flywheel, Zepto has rapidly expanded its product assortment to enhance user engagement, increasing the average number of SKUs at a dark store from 12,312 in FY24 to 46,623 in FY26. This has deepened user adoption, with retained users purchasing from over 18 product categories within two years of joining.

The company has demonstrated strong user base growth, with Annual Transacting Users (ATU) growing from 10.57 million in FY24 to 47.97 million in FY26. This growth is supported by solid user retention, with 45.2% to 49.8% of users remaining active on the platform three years after their first order.

The company is led by its entrepreneurial founders, Aadit Palicha and Kaivalya Vohra, who are deeply involved in granular day-to-day execution. They are supported by an experienced management team with backgrounds in e-commerce, manufacturing, and retail from companies like Flipkart, ITC, and Amazon.

Zepto has rapidly executed its physical infrastructure expansion, growing its network of dark stores from 337 in FY24 to 1,139 in FY26. This aggressive rollout supports its densification strategy and ability to maintain fast delivery times while scaling order volumes.
risks: The company has a history of significant and growing losses, with restated loss for the year increasing from ₹1,214.79 Crores in FY24 to ₹5,905.19 Crores in FY26. It has also consistently generated negative cash flows from operating activities since its inception.

Business growth is critically dependent on acquiring and retaining users, which has historically required significant marketing expenditure. Advertisement expenses increased from ₹303.55 Crores in FY24 to ₹1,389.12 Crores in FY26, representing 6.14% of revenue from operations in the latest fiscal year.

The business model is heavily reliant on a non-exclusive 'gig economy' network of delivery partners and a wide base of merchant partners. In FY26, delivery and handling expenses amounted to ₹3,046.34 Crores, highlighting a major cost center and dependency for its core service.

The company faces intense competition from well-established players and new entrants in a market with low barriers to entry. Key competitors include Blinkit, a subsidiary of the publicly listed Zomato (Eternal Limited), and Instamart, a division of Swiggy, which have deep pockets and established ecosystems.

The company and its Promoters are involved in multiple pending litigations, including a penalty of ₹0.07 Crores from the CCPA for 'dark patterns', which is currently under appeal, and summons received by Promoters from the Directorate of Enforcement regarding FEMA inquiries. Total contingent liabilities from pending litigations are valued at ₹2.01 Crores.

The company experiences very high employee attrition, especially among its operational staff. The overall attrition rate was 51.28% in FY26, while the rate for its crucial 'Operating Staff' (pickers, packers, etc.) was significantly higher at 73.22% for the same period.

profile.overview: Truhome Finance Limited (formerly known as Shriram Housing Finance Limited) is a premier affordable housing finance company (HFC) in India, currently the third-largest in its segment by Assets Under Management (AUM). Following its acquisition by global private equity firm Warburg Pincus in December 2024, the Mumbai-based firm rebranded to Truhome to align with its new strategic positioning. As of December 31, 2025, the company reported an AUM of ₹21,124.32 crore, serving a predominantly self-employed customer base through a pan-India network of 216 branches across 19 states. profile.overview:
Hero Fincorp is a non-banking financial company (NBFC) that provides a range of financial services to retail customers and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in India. Its offerings include vehicle loans (two-wheeler, used car, and electric vehicle loans), personal loans, mortgage loans, and MSME financing (secured and unsecured loans for business needs). Hero Fincorp also offers loans to corporate and institutional customers. 
The company operates under the "Hero" brand and leverages the extensive distribution network of its parent company, Hero MotoCorp, which has a wide dealer presence across India. Hero Fincorp utilises a digital platform for customer acquisition and loan management. 
The company is headquartered in India and has an extensive presence across the country with a combination of in-house teams and distribution partnerships.
Use of proceeds:
The IPO consists of both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS).​ Proceeds from the OFS will go to the respective selling shareholders, whereas the net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​ 
Augmenting the company’s Tier-I capital to support future lending requirements.
Covering expenses related to the offer.

strengths: Hero Fincorp claims to have strategically expanded its product portfolio beyond two-wheeler loans to include a wide range of secured and unsecured loans, catering to both retail and MSME customers. As of FY24, retail and MSME loans accounted for 65.08 percent and 20.80 percent of its total assets under management (AUM).

Hero Fincorp claims to benefit from a deep-rooted relationship with Hero MotoCorp Limited, leveraging its brand recognition and extensive dealer network. In FY24, Hero MotoCorp Limited held a 41.19 percent equity stake in Hero Fincorp and provided financing for a significant portion of Hero MotoCorp’s two-wheeler sales.

The company claims to have developed a comprehensive, omnichannel distribution network that spans 18,603 pin-codes across India, aided by both digital and physical channels. Hero Fincorp also claims to source a substantial portion of its business through partnerships with 3,612 partners, including used car dealers, digital partners, and direct sales agents (DSAs).

Hero Fincorp claims to follow a ‘customer first approach’ that allows it to design customised products for retail and MSME clients, addressing unique financing needs across metro, urban, and rural regions. The company further states this approach enhances cross-sell potential, as demonstrated by a product per customer (PPC) ratio of 4.25 in FY24, 3.15 in FY23, and 3.52 in FY22.

The company claims to integrate technology seamlessly into customer onboarding, underwriting, loan servicing, and collections, providing a fully digital experience. It claims to leverage artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and real-time analytics to improve customer acquisition, reduce wait times, and streamline operations, boosting both operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.

The company claims to have consistently improved its asset quality over the years. As of FY24, the gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio is 4.02 percent, a reduction from 5.11 percent in FY23 and 7.54 percent in 2022. Similarly, the net non-performing assets (NNPA) ratio has declined to 2.00 percent in 2024, compared to 2.69 percent in 2023 and 4.43 percent in 2022.

Leveraging advanced data analytics, Hero Fincorp claims to enhance its risk management by tracking credit trends and predicting default probabilities. It has integrated a technology-driven collections infrastructure, improving efficiency with a 94.42 percent collection rate in FY24, 95.07 percent in FY23, and 83.00 percent in FY22, through mobile app-based repayments and a four-tier collections team.
The company claims to maintain a well-balanced mix of short-term and long-term assets and liabilities, minimising liquidity and interest rate risks.

The company has received credit ratings of AA+ with a stable outlook from Credit Rating Information Services of India Limited (CRISIL), Investment Information and Credit Rating Agency of India Limited (ICRA), and Credit Analysis and Research Limited (CARE), and an A1+ rating for commercial papers from CRISIL, CARE, and ICRA as of FY24.
The company has witnessed a consistent increase in revenue from operations. It increased from Rs 4,738.65 crore in FY22 to Rs 6,401.59 crore in FY23 and Rs 8,290.90 crore in FY24.
risks: Hero Fincorp sourced Rs 9,581.62 crore (99.04 percent), Rs 8,726.52 crore (99.69 percent), and Rs 8,074.88 crore (99.93 percent) of its two-wheeler loans from Hero MotoCorp Limited’s dealerships in FY24, FY23, and FY22, respectively. Any decline in demand for Hero MotoCorp’s two-wheelers could adversely affect the company’s ability to generate revenue from these loans, thereby impacting its business, results of operations, and financial condition.

The company’s retail finance business depends heavily on new-to-credit (NTC) borrowers. They accounted for 8.953.66 crore (26.55 percent) of the company’s total retail AUM in FY24, Rs 8,934.51 crore (34.06 percent) in FY23, and Rs 9,250.4 crore (46.33 percent) in FY22. The lack of credit history makes it difficult to assess these customers’ creditworthiness, which may result in higher default rates. In the event of defaults, recovering these loans, especially unsecured ones, could be challenging, potentially leading to the company’s financial losses.

Retail finance, including vehicle, personal, mortgage, and MSME loans, accounted for Rs 44,506.08 crore (85.88 percent) of the company’s total AUM in FY24, Rs 34,713.74 crore (83.14 percent) in FY23, and Rs 26,117.92 crore (79.02 percent) in FY22. Furthermore, as of FY24, 72.20 percent of these loans are extended to customers in the “Aspiring India” segment, who are vulnerable to economic downturns. Any adverse economic developments could reduce loan demand or increase default rates, negatively impacting the company’s financial condition.
The company’s promoters are involved in certain regulatory proceedings. Any adverse outcomes in these cases could be detrimental to the company’s reputation.

The company’s operations heavily depend on its information technology (IT) systems, which manage risk, deposit servicing, loan origination, and other critical functions. Capital expenditure incurred towards IT systems constituted Rs 48.43 crore (29.48 percent) of the company’s total expenditure in FY24, Rs 26.47 crore (57.51 percent) in FY23, and Rs 18.43 crore (71.79 percent) in FY22. Any internal or external disruptions, system failures, or inadequate maintenance could significantly affect customer service, operations, and the company’s reputation.

The company’s net interest income and margins are vulnerable to fluctuations in interest rates due to its fixed and floating-rate loans and borrowings. As of FY24, FY23, and FY22, Rs 37,084.04 crore (72.03 percent), Rs 31,352.22 crore (75.55 percent), and Rs 25,279.18 crore (76.72 percent) of total gross loans were extended at fixed interest rates. If interest rates rise, the company may not be able to fully pass on increased costs to fixed-rate borrowers, which could lead to lower margins, increased defaults, and reduced loan demand.

As of FY24, FY23, and FY22, unsecured loans accounted for Rs 20,275.58 crore (39.13 percent), Rs 15,521.04 crore (37.18 percent), and Rs 10,497.72 crore (31.76 percent) of the company’s total AUM, respectively. Any failure to recover receivables from these loans could adversely affect the company’s operations, cash flow, and financial condition.

The company is exposed to risks related to the devaluation or loss of collateral backing secured loans, such as property and vehicles. Secured loans accounted for Rs 30,866.24 crore (59.95 percent) of the company’s total gross loans in FY24, Rs 25,928.95 crore (62.48 percent) in FY23, and Rs 22,240.08 crore (67.49 percent) in FY22.

The company relies heavily on third-party distributors, including two-wheeler dealers, digital partners, and direct selling agents (DSAs). They accounted for 62.07 percent, 65.69 percent, and 58.02 percent of the company’s disbursements in FY24, FY23, and FY22, respectively. Any breakdown in relationships, service disruptions, or inefficiencies by these third-party service providers could impact the company’s business operations, financial condition, and reputation.

The company reported negative cash flow from operating activities amounting to Rs 9,238.83 crore in FY24, Rs 6,918.52 crore in FY23, and Rs 5,411.77 crore in FY22. Additionally, negative cash flow from investing activities amounted to Rs 129.79 crore in FY24 and Rs 474.13 crore in FY23. Furthermore, the company experienced a net decrease in cash and cash equivalents amounting to Rs 651.36 crore in FY24, Rs 124.35 crore in FY23, and Rs 232.37 crore in FY22. If cash outflows continue to exceed inflows in the future, the company may face liquidity challenges.
As of June 30, 2024, the company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 43,917.86 crore. Any failure to service or repay these loans can hurt the company’s operations and financial position.

profile.overview:
Antala Industries Limited is engaged in the manufacturing, processing, printing, laminating and supply of industrial and commercial packaging products. The company's product portfolio includes Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene (BOPP) bags, BOPP printing rolls, BOPP lamination rolls, polypropylene (PP) woven bags, and PP woven lamination rolls.
The company supplies packaging products to industries such as food processing, fertilisers, chemicals, cement, construction, textiles, and seeds. Its products are available in different sizes, capacities, and specifications, with customisation options for printing, lamination, and finishing.
The company operates a manufacturing facility in Rajkot, Gujarat, equipped with machinery for extrusion lamination, rotogravure printing, multicolour printing, cutting, stitching, and finishing. The facility supports various stages of production, from printing and lamination to the packaging of finished products.
The company was originally established as a partnership firm under the name M/s Octagon Industries on April 30, 2021, and was subsequently converted into a public limited company under the name Antala Industries Limited on August 5, 2024.

strengths: Antala Industries is engaged in the manufacture of five categories of packaging products, including BOPP bags, BOPP printing rolls, BOPP lamination rolls, PP woven bags, and PP woven lamination rolls. It caters to industries such as cement, chemicals, fertilisers, FMCG, and textiles.

The company has seen a consistent increase in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). The revenue from operations increased from Rs 12.51 crore in FY24 to Rs 31.85 crore in FY25 and Rs 47.40 crore in FY26. Its profit after tax (PAT) also increased from Rs 0.88 crore to Rs 1.82 crore and Rs 4.24 crore during the same periods, respectively.

The company has reported an increase in capacity utilisation across its manufacturing operations. Printing machinery utilisation increased from 20.07% in FY24 to 51.26% in FY25 to 76.05% in FY26, while lamination machinery utilisation rose from 20.23% to 51.68% to 76.67% during the same period. The company's printing machinery installed capacity increased from 330 lakh metres per annum in FY24 to 370.63 lakh metres per annum to 442.50 lakh metres per annum in FY26, while the capacity utilisation during the same period stood at 66.23 lakh metres per annum, 189.98 lakh metres per annum, and 336.50 lakh metres per annum.

The company claims to have an integrated manufacturing facility in Rajkot, Gujarat, equipped with an eight-colour rotogravure printing machine, a flexographic printing machine, automated cutting machinery, and bag conversion lines. The facility supports multiple stages of packaging production.

The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for quality management systems, ISO 14001:2015 for environmental management systems, ISO 45001:2018 for occupational health and safety management systems, and ISO 22000:2018 for food safety management systems.

The company's revenue concentration among its top 10 customers declined from 94.28% (Rs 11.80 crore) in FY24 to 47.43% (Rs 22.48 crore) in FY26. This indicates a more diversified customer base, reducing its dependence on a limited number of customers and the potential impact of losing any major customer on its revenue.
risks: Despite a decline in customer concentration over the years, Antala Industries continues to derive a significant portion of its revenue from its top 10 customers. These customers contributed Rs 11.80 crore (94.28%) in FY24, Rs 14.93 crore (46.87%) in FY25, and Rs 22.48 crore (47.43%) in FY26 to its revenue from operations, respectively. The loss of major customers or a reduction in their orders could adversely affect the company's revenue and profitability.

The company's revenue is geographically concentrated in Gujarat, which accounted for Rs 12.45 crore (99.49%), Rs 25.55 crore (80.22%), and Rs 33.70 crore (71.08%) of its revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Any adverse economic, regulatory or operational developments in the state could significantly affect the company's business and financial performance.

The company depends heavily on Gujarat for raw material procurement. Purchases from the state amounted to Rs 10.73 crore (99.97%), Rs 25.71 crore (96.59%), and Rs 38.66 crore (91.80%) of total raw material purchases in FY24, FY25 and FY26, respectively. Any disruption in regional supply chains could affect production schedules and increase procurement costs.

The company recorded negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 3.28 crore in FY25 and Rs 4.88 crore in FY26, primarily due to increases in inventories, trade receivables, and short-term loans and advances. It also recorded negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 0.03 crore, Rs 0.49 crore, and Rs 1.78 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, and negative cash flow from financing activities of Rs 0.10 crore in FY24. Sustained cash outflows could affect the company's liquidity and ability to meet its operational and financial obligations.

The company operates its manufacturing activities from a single facility in Rajkot, Gujarat, situated on rented premises under a seven-year agreement beginning June 1, 2026. Any disruption at this facility or termination of the lease could interrupt production, affect order fulfilment, and result in additional relocation expenses.

The company has experienced delays in complying with statutory filing requirements under the Companies Act, 2013, including delays of up to 294 days in filing certain forms. It has also filed applications for adjudication concerning procedural non-compliances, which could result in penalties, additional regulatory obligations, or increased scrutiny.

The company's manufacturing operations depend on petroleum-derived raw materials, including polypropylene granules, LDPE granules, and BOPP films. Fluctuations in petrochemical prices, environmental restrictions on plastic-based packaging, or a shift towards alternative packaging materials could increase costs and reduce demand for its products.
As of September 30, 2026, the company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 1.75 crore. Any failure to service or repay these loans can harm the company’s operations and financial position.

Antala Industries derived 63.14% of its revenue from repeat customers in FY26, compared to 39.46% in FY25. For the six months ended September 30, 2026, repeat customers contributed 85.34% of its revenue. Since customer arrangements are generally based on purchase orders without guaranteed future business, the loss of repeat customers or a reduction in their orders could adversely affect the company's revenue, profitability and capacity utilisation.

profile.overview:
Vedant Poly Fabs Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of flexible packaging materials and supplies to business-to-business (B2B) customers across India. Its product portfolio includes 3-layer and 5-layer low-density (LD) films, shrink films, barrier films, printed laminates, and milk and oil pouches used in food and beverage and other consumer product packaging. 
The company manufactures products according to customer specifications, including size, thickness, material composition, and printing requirements. Its manufacturing processes include extrusion, printing, lamination, slitting, and pouching. The facility is equipped with multilayer extrusion machines, central impression (CI) flexographic printing machines, and rotogravure printing machines. 
In addition to manufacturing, the company trades in billet strips used in engineering, fabrication, and manufacturing industries. It commenced operations in 2018 and expanded its manufacturing capacity in March 2026 by adding lamination, slitting, and pouching machines. The company also operates a reprocessing unit to process plastic waste generated during manufacturing for reuse in certain applications.

strengths: The company undertakes extrusion, printing, lamination, slitting, and rewinding at its in-house manufacturing facility. This allows it to manage multiple production stages within a single facility.

The company claims to have an in-house laboratory equipped with testing instruments, including a dart impact tester, coefficient of friction (COF) tester, and universal testing machine. These instruments are used to evaluate film impact resistance, surface characteristics, sealing strength, and tensile strength.

The company’s lamination production increased from 73,648.33 kg in FY24 to 13,60,511.10 kg in FY25 and 30,82,044.37 kg in FY26. This reflects an increase in production volume over the three financial years.

The company manufactures multilayer LD films, printed plastics, milk films, shrink films, printed laminates, and aluminium foil laminates. It added milk and oil printed plastic rolls and printed laminates in 2023, followed by aluminium foil laminates in 2024.

The company claims to operate its own fleet of eight vehicles for delivering finished goods to customers. This allows it to coordinate dispatch schedules internally and reduces its reliance on third-party transportation providers.

The company’s manufacturing facility is located in Barasat, West Bengal, with access to road and rail networks. According to the prospectus, its proximity to certain raw material suppliers and markets in eastern India supports procurement and product distribution.

The company has witnessed a consistent increase in its revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 49.53 crore in FY24 to Rs 81.02 crore in FY25 and Rs 115.14 crore in FY26. PAT increased from Rs 0.63 crore in FY24 to Rs 4.56 crore in FY25 and Rs 10.97 crore in FY26.
risks: The company is dependent on its suppliers for the uninterrupted supply of raw materials, and its top 10 suppliers contributed Rs 88.28 crore (90.16%), Rs 41.35 crore (53.24%), and Rs 16.80 crore (35.13%) of total purchases in FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any disruption in raw material supplies or increase in raw material and other input costs due to price volatility, currency fluctuations, or changes in government policies could adversely affect the company’s production, product pricing, and financial performance.

The company’s top 10 customers contributed Rs 79.95 crore (69.44%), Rs 24.43 crore (30.15%), and Rs 6.68 crore (13.49%) of total sales in FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. profile.overview:

manufacturing facility at Manesar, Gurugram — Rs 15.04  crore

plating facility — Rs 1.05 crore

profile.overview:
Bombay Coated and Special Steels Limited is a steel processing company that converts steel coils into processed steel products for original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and original design manufacturers (ODMs). Its products include slit coils, embossed slit coils, blanks, embossed blanks, and sheared blanks. The company processes coated, hot-rolled, non-coated, and galvanised steel coils for applications in home appliances, automotive manufacturing, electrical equipment, refrigeration, ventilation systems, and pharmaceutical cleanroom infrastructure. It also provides logistics and inventory management services to support the supply of processed steel products to customers.
The company operates four manufacturing facilities located in Wada and Bhiwandi in Maharashtra, Ghiloth in Rajasthan, and Sri City in Andhra Pradesh. These facilities are equipped with slitting, cut-to-length, shearing, and embossing lines. As of June 30, 2026, the company had an aggregate installed processing capacity of 123,153 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA). Since 2021, it has been an authorised service partner of JSW Steel Coated Products Limited.
profile.productsAndServices: Bombay Coated and Special Steels operates in its core segment.
profile.businessModel: Mainboard issue (Book Built) listed on NSE / BSE.
profile.industryOverview: Sector primary market offering tracked via SEBI & exchange filings.
profile.competitivePosition: Consolidated subscription recorded at 63.89x.
strengths: The company has been an authorised service partner of JSW Steel Coated Products Limited (JSWSCPL) since 2021. JSWSCPL accounted for 85.13%, 86.65%, 90.61%, and 84.58% of the company’s total steel coil purchases in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and original design manufacturers (ODMs), including Haier Appliances India, IFB Refrigeration, Amber Enterprises India, Dixon Electro Manufacturing and Western Refrigeration. Revenue from existing customers accounted for 98.05%, 96.08%, 93.76% and 87.88% of revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and FY26, FY25 and FY24, respectively.

The company operates manufacturing facilities in Wada and Bhiwandi in Maharashtra, Ghiloth in Rajasthan, and Sri City in Andhra Pradesh. Their locations near industrial clusters and customer manufacturing units support regional supply and reduce transportation time and costs.

The company claims to have processing infrastructure comprising slitting, cut-to-length, shearing, and embossing lines. As of June 30, 2026, its installed capacities included 123,153 MTPA for slitting, 50,481 MTPA for cut-to-length processing, 1,467 MTPA for shearing, and 11,700 MTPA for embossing.

The company’s manufacturing facilities are ISO 9001:2015 certified for quality management systems. The company also states that it follows quality control procedures established jointly with JSWSCPL to maintain product specifications and consistency.
As of June 30, 2026, the company served 178 customers across home and commercial appliances, automotive, electrical equipment, refrigeration, ventilation and other industrial sectors.

The company has shown a consistent increase in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT) in FY24, FY25, and FY26. Revenue from operations increased from Rs 752.26 crore in FY24 to Rs 1,055.71 crore in FY25 to Rs 1,266.82 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 21.14 crore to Rs 28.67 crore and Rs 30.54 crore over the same period.
risks: The company depends substantially on JSW Steel Coated Products Ltd (JSWSCPL) for its steel coil requirements. JSWSCPL accounted for Rs 239.77 crore (85.13%) of total steel coil purchases in the three months ended June 30, 2026; Rs 1,034.21 crore (86.65%) in FY26; Rs 869.18 crore (90.61%) in FY25; and Rs 557.94 crore (84.58%) in FY24. Any disruption in supplies, adverse changes in commercial terms, or termination of the authorised service partner arrangement could affect the company’s production, customer deliveries, and profitability.

The company reported negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 0.68 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 35.03 crore in FY26, Rs 41.76 crore in FY25, and Rs 52.85 crore in FY24. These outflows were primarily due to purchases of capital assets and increases in other non-current financial assets and other non-current assets, partly offset by changes in fixed or restricted bank deposits, proceeds from the sale of capital assets, and interest income. The company also reported negative cash flows from financing activities of Rs 73.34 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with positive cash flows of Rs 33.71 crore in FY26, Rs 11.57 crore in FY25 and Rs 39.56 crore in FY24. Any continued negative cash flows could affect the company’s ability to meet working capital requirements, service its debt, fund capital expenditure and implement expansion plans without raising additional funds, which may adversely affect its business and financial condition.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from its top 10 customers, which contributed Rs 292.01 crore (73.54%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 903.60 crore (71.33%) in FY26, Rs 712.01 crore (67.44%) in FY25, and Rs 509.28 crore (67.43%) in FY24. Any loss of key customers or reduction in orders due to commercial disputes, financial difficulties, lower demand or operational disruptions could adversely affect the company’s revenue, financial condition and cash flows.

The cost of raw materials and components consumed accounted for Rs 330.17 crore (87.60% of total expenses) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 1,112.37 crore (90.51%) in FY26, Rs 949.71 crore (92.97%) in FY25 and Rs 657.11 crore (89.14%) in FY24. The company is exposed to fluctuations in steel coil prices and supply disruptions, which could increase production costs, affect profit margins, and delay customer deliveries. Any inability to pass on higher costs to customers or procure sufficient steel coils at commercially acceptable prices could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company had a debt-to-equity ratio of 2 times as of June 30, 2026, compared with 2.78 times in FY26, 3.33 times in FY25, and 4.31 times in FY24. Its debt obligations expose it to interest costs, reduced financial flexibility, and risks arising from changes in interest rates or non-compliance with loan covenants. Inability to service debt obligations or refinance borrowings on favourable terms could adversely affect the company’s liquidity, financial condition and ability to fund its growth plans.

The company, its promoters, directors, and certain members of the promoter group are involved in outstanding legal and regulatory proceedings. Any adverse outcome in these proceedings could hurt the company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows. However, no criminal or regulatory proceedings are pending against its key managerial personnel or senior management as of the date of the red herring prospectus.

The company had consolidated outstanding borrowings of Rs 302.43 crore as of August 31, 2026. The company’s indebtedness and related financing obligations could increase its financial costs and affect its cash flows and financial condition.

As of June 30, 2026, Bombay Coated and Special Steels Limited had trade receivables amounting to Rs 165.41 crore. Any failure to collect these receivables on time or at all could adversely affect the company’s cash flows and financial condition.

profile.overview:
̌Carver Roboweld Limited is a manufacturer of welding consumables and provides engineering services to the forging industry. Its products include metal-cored wires, welding rods, gauging electrodes, welding spare parts, and accessories used in welding operations and equipment maintenance. The company also offers forging die regeneration and welding robot rental services.
Its subsidiary, Carver Engineering Private Limited, provides reconditioning and refurbishment services for plant and machinery across industries such as forging, casting, cement, steel, sugar, power, petroleum, automotive, and fabrication. Its services include hammer and component repairs, structural fabrication, machining, and turnkey engineering projects.
The company’s primary manufacturing facility is located in Rajkot, Gujarat. It also operates service units in Pune, Hosur, and Ludhiana. As of July 11, 2026, its installed annual production capacity for metal-cored wires and welding rods was 650 tonnes. The company sources raw materials from domestic suppliers and international markets, including China, the United States, and the Netherlands.

The company operates a manufacturing facility in Bamanbore, Rajkot, Gujarat, and service units in Pune, Ludhiana, and Hosur. This network enables it to serve customers across western, southern, and northern India.

The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for the sales of welding consumables, including welding electrodes and metal-cored wires, and for the manufacturing and supply of welding electrodes. It is also a Sustaining Corporate Member of the American Welding Society (AWS).

Any slowdown in the forging industry or decline in demand from end-user sectors such as automotive, infrastructure, and engineering could adversely affect the company’s revenue and profitability.

A substantial portion of the company’s revenue comes from Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu. profile.overview:
M. K. Sons Fine Jewels Limited is a retail jewellery company that sells gold, diamond, and cubic zirconia (CZ) jewellery through its chain of showrooms.
The company's product portfolio includes rings, earrings, necklaces, chains, bangles, bracelets, pendants, mangalsutras, and other jewellery items for everyday wear, weddings, and other occasions. As of June 30, 2026, the company had 19,442 stock-keeping units (SKUs), comprising over 14,582 gold jewellery designs and 4,860 designs featuring diamonds and other precious stones. It also offers customised jewellery designs, gemstone selections, and personalised engravings.
The company operates five company-owned, company-operated (COCO) retail showrooms, of which three are in Mumbai and two in Ahmedabad, with a total operational area of 6,513 square feet. It primarily procures finished jewellery from third-party manufacturers and wholesalers in Maharashtra and Gujarat, while also working with Karigars and an in-house design team for select jewellery designs.

strengths: The company offers jewellery across 11 distinct collections, covering gold, diamond and cubic zirconia (CZ) jewellery. Its collections include traditional bridal jewellery, everyday wear, men's jewellery, religious jewellery and customised designs, with approximate prices ranging from Rs 11,000 to Rs 85 lakh.

The company has recorded consistent growth in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 217.32 crore in FY24 to Rs 351.28 crore in FY25 and Rs 538.74 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 8.17 crore to Rs 23.26 crore and Rs 51.80 crore, respectively.

The company has expanded its customer base, with the number of unique customers increasing from 12,042 in FY24 to 18,000 in FY25 and 24,274 in FY26. The number of new customers also increased from 11,787 to 15,821 and 21,952, respectively.

The company has established a presence across digital platforms, with over 5.91 lakh followers on Instagram, 76,800 subscribers on YouTube and 43,000 followers on Pinterest as of the RHP date. It also participated in 16 exhibitions during FY26 and undertakes advertising campaigns targeting customers across more than 18 Indian states.

The company claims to have an internal inventory management system that enables real-time stock monitoring, barcode tracking, inter-branch transfers, and stock reconciliation across its showrooms. It also uses Tally ERP to record purchases, sales, stock movements, and inventory valuations.

The company deals in gold jewellery certified under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) hallmarking requirements. It also states that its diamond jewellery is accompanied by certifications from gemological laboratories such as the International Gemological Institute (IGI) and/or the Gemological Institute of America (GIA).
risks: The company's revenue from its Gujarat showrooms stood at Rs 162.54 crore, Rs 271.10 crore, and Rs 366.16 crore, accounting for 74.79%, 77.17%, and 67.97% of total revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Its C.G. Road showroom in Ahmedabad alone generated Rs 307.95 crore in FY26, accounting for 57.16% of total revenue. Any adverse developments affecting Gujarat or the C.G. Road showroom could significantly impact the company's revenue, profitability, and overall financial performance.

The company generated its entire revenue from operations of Rs 217.32 crore, Rs 351.28 crore, and Rs 538.74 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively, through five physical showrooms. With no revenue from online sales or alternative distribution channels, any decline in customer footfall or disruption to showroom operations could directly affect its financial performance.

The company relies entirely on third-party manufacturers and Karigars for jewellery production, without long-term contractual arrangements or exclusive manufacturing relationships. Any supply disruption, production delays, or unauthorised disclosure of jewellery designs could adversely affect its operations, profitability, and financial performance.

The company recorded negative cash flows from operating activities amounting to Rs 23.55 crore and Rs 9.53 crore in FY24 and FY25, respectively, primarily due to increased inventory and working capital requirements. It also recorded negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 0.87 crore, Rs 2.34 crore, and Rs 2.93 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively, primarily due to capital expenditure on the purchase of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets; and negative cash flows from financing activities of Rs 9.77 crore in FY26, primarily due to lease principal repayments and finance costs. Sustained cash outflows exceeding inflows could adversely affect the company's liquidity and financial position.

The company's working capital gap increased from Rs 60.49 crore in FY24 to Rs 183.15 crore in FY25 and Rs 240.49 crore in FY26. As of June 30, 2026, its outstanding borrowings stood at Rs 70.52 crore, while its working capital gap reached Rs 266.38 crore. Any inability to secure additional financing on favourable terms could affect its operations and expansion plans.

The company had a portfolio of over 19,442 jewellery SKUs as of June 30, 2026, but its designs were not registered under the Designs Act, 2000. This could limit its ability to prevent competitors from replicating its designs or pursuing legal remedies against unauthorised copying.

The company's inventories increased from Rs 87.48 crore in FY24 to Rs 205.70 crore in FY25 and Rs 256.43 crore in FY26, reaching Rs 275.23 crore as of June 30, 2026. Its inventory holding period increased from 122 days in FY24 to 178 days in FY25 and 193 days in FY26, reaching 333 days for the three months ended June 30, 2026, on a non-annualised basis. High inventory levels and long inventory holding periods could increase working capital requirements and financing costs.

The company's revenue during the third and fourth quarters collectively stood at Rs 173.95 crore, Rs 205.86 crore, and Rs 357.07 crore, accounting for 80.04%, 58.61%, and 66.28% of annual revenue in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. A decline in jewellery demand during weddings and festive seasons could disproportionately affect its annual financial performance.

Revenue from gold jewellery stood at Rs 194.35 crore, Rs 298.39 crore, and Rs 471.08 crore, contributing 89.43%, 84.94%, and 87.44% of revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Since gold jewellery generally carries lower margins than diamond-studded and designer jewellery, continued dependence on gold sales could constrain the company's profitability.

profile.overview:
Ajwa Projects Limited provides industrial engineering, fabrication, erection, piping, maintenance, and civil construction services. The company undertakes structural fabrication work involving industrial buildings, girders, platforms, heavy modules, and other steel structures. It also manufactures equipment such as pressure vessels, boilers, heat exchangers, tanks, chimneys, ducts, and specialised industrial components.
The company's services include installing and assembling industrial structures, equipment, and piping systems. It also undertakes civil construction activities, including site preparation, earthworks, foundations, factory buildings, and supporting infrastructure. The company also provides prefabricated structures, mechanical maintenance, non-destructive testing, sandblasting, and industrial painting services.
Ajwa Projects serves industries including oil and gas, refineries, power generation, steel, cement, chemicals, and transportation infrastructure. The company operates a workshop facility at Ichchapore GIDC in Surat, Gujarat, and carries out fabrication and installation activities at client project sites.

profile.overview:
BLS Polymers is a manufacturer of custom-formulated polymer compounds used in the wire and cable, infrastructure, and other industries. Its products are used for insulation, sheathing, jacketing, and protective coating of wires, cables, and underground pipelines. The company’s product portfolio includes high-density polyethylene (HDPE), medium-density polyethylene (MDPE), linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE), cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE), halogen-free flame-retardant (HFFR), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), cable filling compounds (CFC), and adhesive coating compounds. 
These products are used in applications across the power, telecommunications, railways, water, and oil and gas distribution industries. HDPE, MDPE, and LLDPE compounds are used in wire and cable insulation and protection, while XLPE, HFFR, PVC, and CFC compounds serve applications requiring properties such as electrical insulation, fire resistance, and moisture resistance. HDPE and adhesive coating compounds are also used in three-layer polyethylene (3LPE) coatings for oil, gas, and water pipelines.

strengths: BLS Polymers has enlisted several products with government agencies and public sector enterprises, including a Maharatna CPSE power transmission company, a Navratna CPSE engineering consultancy company, a Miniratna CPSE telecommunications company, and the Government of Gujarat. These approvals cover products used in wire and cable manufacturing, oil and gas pipelines, and water pipelines.

As of August 31, 2026, the company manufactured six product categories across 127 grades, including PE, XLPE, PVC, CFC, HFFR, and pipe coating compounds. These products cater to applications in power cables, telecommunications, railway signalling, and oil, gas, and water distribution pipelines.

As of August 31, 2026, BLS Polymers has an in-house product development team of seven employees. The team has developed pipe coating adhesives for underground oil, gas, and water pipelines, and the products have received certification from Bureau Veritas for compliance with standards including ISO 21809-1:2018 and DIN 30670:2012.

The company sold its products in 23 states and Union Territories during the three months ended June 30, 2026, and the preceding three financial years. Its domestic operations accounted for 94.68% of revenue from operations during the three months ended June 30, 2026.

The company has shown a consistent increase in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT) in FY24, FY25, and FY26. Revenue from operations increased from Rs 296.36 crore in FY24 to Rs 328.43 crore in FY25 to Rs 349.43 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 7.52 crore to Rs 21.14 crore and Rs 27.01 crore over the same period.
risks: The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from the sale of wire and cable polymer compounds, which contributed Rs 78.34 crore (73.20%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 282.80 crore (80.93%) in FY26, Rs 267.98 crore (81.59%) in FY25, and Rs 238.53 crore (80.49%) in FY24. A reduction in demand for these products, a downturn in the wire and cable industry, or an inability to diversify its product portfolio and retain customers could adversely affect the company’s revenue, profitability, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from its top 10 customers, who contributed Rs 65.65 crore (61.34%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 233.47 crore (66.81%) in FY26, Rs 211.67 crore (64.44%) in FY25, and Rs 149.74 crore (50.52%) in FY24. Any loss of these customers, reduction or cancellation of orders, or inability to maintain existing order volumes and pricing terms could adversely affect the company’s revenue, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.

The company reported negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 4.08 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 5.79 crore during the same period. Negative investing cash flows were also reported in FY26, FY24, and the three months ended June 30, 2026, primarily due to additions to property, plant and equipment, including plant and machinery to increase production capacity. The company also reported negative cash flows from financing activities of Rs 31.05 crore in FY26, Rs 25.72 crore in FY25, and Rs 2.24 crore in FY24, mainly due to repayments of unsecured loans from a group company and working capital demand loans, as well as higher interest payments on bank borrowings in FY24. Sustained or significant negative cash flows in the future could adversely affect the company’s financial condition, operations, and growth plans.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from repeat orders, which contributed Rs 97.23 crore (90.84%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 337.24 crore (96.51%) in FY26, Rs 305.57 crore (93.04%) in FY25, and Rs 241.98 crore (81.65%) in FY24. Its ability to retain repeat orders depends on maintaining product quality, competitive pricing, and timely deliveries. Failure to meet customer requirements, urgent demand, or quality expectations, disputes, termination of existing arrangements, or deterioration in customers’ financial conditions could reduce repeat orders and adversely affect the company’s revenue, profitability, financial condition, and cash flows. Acquiring new customers also involves additional marketing and onboarding expenses.

The company depends on a limited number of suppliers for key raw materials, including LLDPE resin, HDPE resin, and recycled HDPE, which accounted for 76.62% of revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026, 78.13% in FY26, 80.85% in FY25, and 83.90% in FY24. Its top 10 suppliers accounted for 88.02% of total procurement costs during the three months ended June 30, 2026, 93.52% in FY26, 83.52% in FY25, and 75.34% in FY24. profile.overview:
SFC Environmental Technologies Ltd is an environmental technology company incorporated in 2005. The company provides technologies and engineering solutions for wastewater treatment, wastewater recycling and reuse, and solid waste treatment.
Its wastewater treatment operations include designing, manufacturing, supplying, supervising installation, and commissioning treatment equipment. It uses its proprietary C-Tech technology to treat sewage and effluents. The company also offers turbo blowers, fibre disc filters, solar sludge drying systems, and membrane-based treatment technologies. Its wastewater recycling and reuse solutions include ultrafiltration, closed-circuit reverse osmosis, and membrane bioreactor technologies.
In solid waste treatment, the company provides plant design, engineering, construction, installation, commissioning, and operations and maintenance services. Its proprietary OREX technology separates biodegradable organic matter from inorganic materials in municipal solid waste. The company operates two integrated solid waste treatment facilities in Goa, with a combined treatment capacity of 350 tonnes per day and an additional handling capacity of 75 tonnes per day. Through its subsidiaries, it is also involved in compressed biogas projects using municipal and agricultural waste.

Planned compressed biogas and waste-to-energy projects may also require further equity or capital investments, with funding amounts and timelines yet to be determined. profile.overview:
Wiscon Industries Limited is a Delhi-based supplier of consumer electronic products in India. Its product portfolio includes LED televisions, air coolers, washing machines, and air conditioners, which are sold under its flagship brand, Wiscon. The company also sells electric scooters under a third-party brand.
The company serves both business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) customers. It conducts its B2B operations through an offline customer network, while it makes B2C sales through its website. Wiscon Industries was incorporated as a public limited company on September 16, 2022. 
In May 2025, the company acquired a 100% stake in Dalmia Technologies Limited (DTL), which manufactures LED televisions and trades in other electronic products. DTL became its wholly owned subsidiary, and the company’s consolidated financial statements include DTL from FY26 onward. Accordingly, consolidated figures for FY26 and the quarter ended June 30, 2026 include DTL’s financial results, while historical figures for FY24 and FY25 in the relevant standalone statements reflect Wiscon Industries on a standalone basis.

Investment in the wholly owned subsidiary, Dalmia Technologies Limited for financing its capital expenditure towards purchase of plant and machinery — Rs 15.04 crore
Investment in Dalmia Technologies Limited for funding its incremental working capital requirements — Rs 35 crore
To meet working capital requirements of Wiscon— Rs 17 crore
To fund marketing and promotional activities in the company — Rs 5.22 crore
General corporate purposes

profile.overview:
Jio Platforms is a technology company that provides digital connectivity and digital services across India. Its subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited, offers mobile connectivity, fixed broadband, and digital services. These services provide access to the internet, digital applications, and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI). 
The company develops and operates its own technology stack, covering network infrastructure, device engineering, software, operating systems, and digital applications. Its technology portfolio includes 4G, 5G, cloud-native core network architectures, and AI-driven network automation. The company also develops digital products and technologies for consumers and businesses. 
As of June 30, 2026, Jio Platforms and its subsidiaries had applied for 7,220 patents in India and other countries across various digital technology areas. The company had 12,477 employees in its digital products and technology development team as of the same date. Its business combines digital connectivity infrastructure with software, applications, and other digital services.
Use of proceeds: 
This is a fresh issue of shares. Therefore, the net proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company. They will be utilised for the following purposes:
Prepayment, in full or in part, of certain outstanding borrowings availed by the material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL) — Rs 27,500 crore
General corporate purposes

The company claims to operate an end-to-end 5G standalone technology stack nationwide, covering its core network, devices, and OSS/BSS operating systems. It also uses proprietary unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology to provide fixed wireless broadband connectivity, with bandwidth of up to 1 Gbps.

Jio Platforms offers consumer applications such as MyJio, JioTV+, JioSaavn, JioAICloud, and JioGames, along with business solutions such as managed Wi-Fi and hybrid cloud services. As of June 30, 2026, JioTV+ aggregated over 1,000 digital TV channels and 15 OTT services.

The company uses its proprietary AI platform, JioBrain, for network capacity allocation, fault prediction, anomaly detection, and network optimisation. It also uses digital twin technology to assess network coverage, plan infrastructure rollouts, and guide field engineers during customer installations.
The company reported revenue from operations of Rs 146,885.3 crore and EBITDA of Rs 76,255.4 crore in FY26. Its net leverage ratio declined from 0.88 times in FY24 to 0.36 times in FY26.
risks: Jio Platforms has entered into various agreements with Reliance Industries Limited, Reliance Retail Limited, and other Reliance Group entities for project execution, business support, equipment supply, and distribution services. Reliance Retail Limited is the sole distributor of the company’s prepaid connectivity services, which contributed 76.37%, 77.88%, 77.08%, 78.57%, and 79.35% of consolidated revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any disruption or termination of these arrangements could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL), the company’s material subsidiary, contributed 87.74% of consolidated revenue from operations, 94.88% of EBITDA, and 93.76% of profit after tax in FY26. Any deterioration in RJIL’s business or financial performance due to competition, regulatory changes, technological disruption, or other adverse events could materially affect the company’s consolidated financial results. Further, the company’s key performance indicators primarily reflect RJIL’s digital connectivity services and may not adequately represent its technology platform business, potentially limiting investors’ ability to assess its performance in this area.

Jio Platforms depends on a limited number of service providers for passive network infrastructure. As of June 30, 2026, Summit Digitel Infrastructure Limited owned 174,451 of the 360,537 network towers used by the company, while Jio Digital Fibre Private Limited met approximately 98% of its optic fibre network requirements, excluding the last-mile fibre network owned by RJIL. RJIL has long-term agreements with both providers, which require minimum payments and do not permit termination by RJIL. Any disruption in tower or fibre availability, failure to meet service commitments, or relocation of infrastructure could cause network outages, service degradation, and customer losses, adversely affecting the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms’ systems, networks, applications, and data may be exposed to cybersecurity threats, including ransomware, phishing, malware, and data or privacy breaches. Although the company reported no successful cyberattacks or security breaches during the three months ended June 30, 2026, or FY24 to FY26, future incidents could require significant expenditure to investigate and resolve, disrupt operations, and damage its reputation. The company also relies on data centre infrastructure provided by its promoter in Jamnagar, Nagpur, and Mumbai, as well as third-party cloud hosting and edge infrastructure services. Any disruption or termination of these arrangements could affect service quality, increase customer churn, and adversely affect the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms’ telecommunications business is subject to extensive and evolving regulations covering licensing, spectrum usage, data privacy, and digital services. RJIL faces regulatory demands, including Rs 27.1 crore in financial disincentives imposed by TRAI for alleged violations relating to unsolicited commercial communications and service quality, which are under appeal. RJIL also faces a disputed additional spectrum usage charge demand of Rs 138.91 crore, which was set aside by TDSAT but is subject to an appeal before the Supreme Court. The company has previously incurred Rs 123.2 crore in non-performance penalties and liquidated damages for prolonged service interruptions in specified locations. Changes in licence fees, spectrum charges or other regulations, or failure to comply with applicable requirements, could increase costs, result in penalties or restrict services, adversely affecting the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms operates a capital-intensive business, with cash capital expenditure of Rs 34,184.3 crore in FY26, Rs 44,268 crore in FY25 and Rs 53,509.6 crore in FY24, representing 23.27%, 34.53% and 48.84% of revenue from operations, respectively. In FY26, network expenditure accounted for Rs 29,377.1 crore of cash capital expenditure. Significant spending on network expansion, technology upgrades, and digital platforms may take time to generate returns and depends on regulatory approvals, funding availability, and customer adoption. Cost overruns, delays, or lower-than-expected demand for new services could reduce the returns on these investments and adversely affect the company’s financial performance.

Fifteen subsidiaries of Jio Platforms incurred losses during the three months ended June 30, 2026, with combined losses after tax of Rs 20.5 crore. In FY26, 11 subsidiaries reported combined losses after tax of Rs 100.6 crore, compared with Rs 162.8 crore in FY25 and Rs 57.4 crore in FY24. Although these losses were not material to the company’s consolidated financial results during these periods, continued losses may require additional financial support or equity infusions by the company and could adversely affect its financial condition and results of operations.

profile.overview:

The company aggregates manufacturing capacity through a network of third-party suppliers and its own facilities, supported by its proprietary technology platform, Zetwerk OS. Its third-party supplier network spans several countries, including India, Vietnam, Thailand, Taiwan, Germany, Spain, Mexico and the USA. Zetwerk serves customers ranging from startups to established companies across various industries. Ltd.; (viii) Zap91 Solar India Private Limited; and (ix) Zet Town India Private Limited through investments in such them — Rs 1,300 crore

profile.overview:
Sahajanand Medical Technologies Limited develops, manufactures, and sells medical devices used in vascular and structural heart interventions. Founded in 2001, the company offers vascular intervention products, including coronary stents and coronary balloon catheters, and structural heart products, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) devices and occluders. Its portfolio also includes renal stents, peripheral drug-coated balloons, and traded medical products.
The company markets its products through direct sales, hybrid, and distributor-led models. In FY26, it generated revenue from 77 countries, including India, with operations across Europe and other international markets. It currently operates three manufacturing facilities, two in India and one in Thailand. Additionally, it has two research and development centres, located in India and Thailand, focused on medical device development and product improvements.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO is an offer-for-sale (OFS). The company will not receive any proceeds from the offer. Net proceeds from the offer will go to the promoter selling shareholders in proportion to the number of shares offered by them for sale.
The primary objective of the offer is to achieve the benefits of listing the equity shares on the stock exchanges, which is expected to enhance the company’s visibility and brand recognition. Listing will also provide liquidity to the existing shareholders and create a public market for the company’s shares in India​.

The company supplies its products to government defence agencies, law enforcement and homeland security agencies, and other defence equipment manufacturers in India and overseas.
The company operates an R&D centre in Bengaluru, Karnataka, where it undertakes product design, development and prototyping. Listing will also provide liquidity to the existing shareholders and create a public market for the company’s shares in India.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from tactical systems, which contributed Rs 359.27 crore (83.90%), Rs 362.30 crore (77.24%), and Rs 211.67 crore (58.37%) to revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Any decline in demand for these products could adversely affect its revenue and profitability.

The company recorded negative cash flows from operating activities amounting to Rs 136.12 crore and Rs 63.22 crore in FY25 and FY26, respectively, and Rs 14.68 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026. The negative cash flows in FY25 were primarily due to an increase in trade receivables and other non-current financial assets, along with a decrease in other current liabilities related to the one-time intellectual property acquisition in FY24. In FY26 and the three months ended June 30, 2026, the outflows were mainly attributable to increased inventory requirements, changes in other current assets and provisions, and working capital adjustments. Continued negative operating cash flows could create liquidity challenges for the company.

The company incurred liquidated damages amounting to Rs 21.82 crore, Rs 18.93 crore, and Rs 3.80 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively, due to delays in meeting contractual delivery schedules. Its defence contracts also contain stringent warranty obligations, and further delays or product defects could result in additional penalties and replacement costs.

The company depends significantly on its Bengaluru R&D centre, where it designs and develops pilot engineering units before outsourcing large-scale manufacturing. Any adverse political, social or economic developments in Karnataka, or disruptions at this facility, could negatively affect its product development and business operations.
As of August 31, 2026, the company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 246.25 crore. Any failure to service or repay these loans can harm the company’s operations and financial position.

profile.overview:
Shellz manufactures and markets confectionery products and supplies food and bakery ingredients. Its product portfolio includes over 300 stock keeping units (SKUs) across categories such as baked treats, chocolates, jellies, panned confectionery and sugar confectionery. The company markets its consumer products under the brands Hugs and Tosca. It also manufactures products under private labels for third-party customers and exports to markets in the Middle East, South Asia, and Europe. 
In addition, it supplies non-branded food and bakery ingredients. The company operates through a distribution network of over 300 super stockists, with its products available across retail outlets in around 24 states in India as of March 31, 2026. Its manufacturing facilities are located in Delhi and Sonipat, Haryana. The Sonipat facility is being developed to consolidate and expand existing operations and increase production capacity. The company manufactures its consumer products in-house.
profile.productsAndServices: Shellz India Ltd operates in FMCG (Founded 2012).
profile.businessModel: SME issue (FP) listed on BSE · ISIN INE0Z7301016.
profile.industryOverview: FMCG primary market offering tracked via SEBI & exchange filings.
profile.competitivePosition: Stock listed on 23 October
strengths: Shellz offers products across categories such as baked treats, choco delights, jellies, panned confectionery and sugar candies. It has developed products such as Dip Sticks, which combine biscuit sticks with chocolate cream, and Push Up, a cone-based cream and biscuit snack. Its Tosca brand also includes Tosca Oat Choco, an oat and cereal-based product.

A majority of the company’s SKUs are priced at Rs 10 or below. Its products cater to mass-market consumers across different consumption occasions, while the Tosca brand targets the relatively higher-priced mass-premium segment.

As of March 31, 2026, Shellz had a network of over 300 super stockists, with its products available across retail outlets in around 24 states in India. Its distribution model relies on super stockists and distributors to reach urban, semi-urban and rural markets.

The company manufactures its consumer products in-house at its production facilities in Delhi and Sonipat, Haryana. It claims that its manufacturing setup supports multiple confectionery categories and formats, with machinery sourced from countries including Turkey, China, and Indonesia. The Sonipat facility is being developed to consolidate existing operations and expand production capacity.

Shellz claims to have a team of food and packaging technologists involved in product formulation, ingredient selection, product trials, and packaging design. Its product development process includes evaluating taste, stability, manufacturability, and shelf life before commercialisation.

The company has witnessed a consistent increase in its revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 162.41 crore in FY24 to Rs 186.97 crore in FY25 and Rs 192.61 crore in FY26. PAT increased from Rs 5.25 crore in FY24 to Rs 8.30 crore in FY25 and Rs 13.37 crore in FY26.
risks: The company, its subsidiaries, group companies, promoters, directors, key managerial personnel and senior managerial personnel are involved in certain ongoing legal proceedings. Any adverse decisions in these cases could negatively affect the company’s business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

The company has faced litigation involving vendors and suppliers, including cases related to unpaid dues and cheque dishonour. It does not have long-term supply agreements with most suppliers and sourced raw materials from 132 suppliers in the three months ended June 30, 2026, 249 suppliers in FY26, 218 suppliers in FY25 and 212 suppliers in FY24. Any disruption in supplier relationships or raw material procurement could affect its manufacturing operations and financial performance.

The company recorded negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 11.30 crore in FY26 and negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 12.43 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 7.02 crore in FY26, Rs 30.53 crore in FY25, and Rs 3.93 crore in FY24. Negative operating cash flow in FY26 was primarily due to advance payments of Rs 26.77 crore to suppliers, while negative investing cash flow in the three months ended June 30, 2026, was mainly due to fixed asset purchases of Rs 12.45 crore for the new manufacturing facility at Sonipat. If negative cash flows persist, the company may struggle to fund its operations and implement its growth plans.

The company’s cost of materials consumed stood at Rs 35.05 crore, Rs 128.25 crore, Rs 156.90 crore, and Rs 141.63 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. These costs accounted for 84.27%, 73.76%, 89.77%, and 91.47% of total expenses in the respective periods. Any increase in raw material prices that the company cannot pass on to customers could put pressure on its profit margins.

The company had contingent liabilities of Rs 24.87 crore as of June 30, 2026. Any adverse outcome or materialisation of these liabilities could affect the company’s financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

The company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 109.49 crore as of June 30, 2026. Any failure to service or repay its borrowings on time could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company had trade receivables of Rs 53.89 crore as of June 30, 2026. Any delay or failure in collecting these receivables could increase working capital requirements and adversely affect the company’s cash flows and financial condition.

profile.overview:
Bonfiglioli Transmissions Limited manufactures mechanical and electro-mechanical power transmission products and industrial drive systems. The company is part of the Italy-based Bonfiglioli Group and has been operating in India for over 25 years.
The company operates across three business verticals: Industry & Automation Solutions, Off-Highway Mobility Industry, and Wind Industry. Its product portfolio includes gear motors, gearboxes, electric motors, variable frequency drives, servo motors, precision drives for robotics and automation, swing and track drives, wheel and conveyor drives, and yaw and pitch drives for wind turbines. These products are used across industries such as material handling, mining, construction, agriculture, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, food processing, textiles, and renewable energy.
The company operates three manufacturing facilities in India, located at Thirumudivakkam and Mannur in Tamil Nadu, and Talegaon in Maharashtra. It also has 13 sales offices across India.
profile.productsAndServices: Bonfiglioli Transmissions Ltd operates in Engineering (Founded 1998).
profile.businessModel: Mainboard issue (EQUITY) listed on NSE / BSE · ISIN INE28SO01013.
